name: A small guide to a shared garden
introduction: Five little chapters for making a place where people and plants can grow together.

sections.title: Begin with a conversation
sections.body:
Ask what people would like to grow, and what they already know. A shared garden begins with listening.

Make space for someone who has never held a trowel. One friendly invitation can change how a place feels.

Write down a small first step that everyone can recognise.

sections.title: Find a patch of possibility
sections.body:
Notice the light, the path to water, and the places where people already gather. Walk around at a few different times of day.

A modest space that is easy to reach can be more useful than a beautiful place that is hard to visit.

Agree who can help care for the space before planting begins.

sections.title: Plant something forgiving
sections.body:
Choose a few plants suited to the place and the season. Leave room between them, and room for questions.

Keep the first planting small enough to care for together. Mark what went where; a pencil and a simple label are enough.

Give someone new the chance to plant the first seed.

sections.title: Make care a shared rhythm
sections.body:
A clear watering plan is kinder than a hopeful guess. Decide how people will notice when a task needs doing.

Share what worked as well as what did not. Leave a short note for the next person, and make it easy to ask for help.

A garden changes. Let the plan change with it.

sections.title: Share what grows
sections.body:
Celebrate the small things: a new leaf, a useful conversation, a person returning for a second visit.

Share the harvest with people who helped and people who are curious. Keep a little space for a new idea next season.

The garden is a place to grow things, and a place to belong.
